stories.title: Iran gloats over Trump’s midterm blowout: ‘US collapse has accelerated’
stories.dek: Iranian officials mocked President Trump over Republicans' midterm losses and warned that the regime would deploy "new weapons" if he chooses to restart the war.
stories.content:
Iranian officials mocked President Trump over Republicans’ midterm losses and warned that the regime would deploy “new weapons” if he chooses to restart the war.

“Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and ‌we endorse this message,” Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf gloated on X, warning Trump against resuming the conflict.

“If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” the chief Iranian negotiator added.

Hamidreza Moghadamfar, an adviser to the Commander-in-Chief of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), also warned that Tehran was ready to respond if Trump makes good on his promise to renew airstrikes after the midterms.

“If the United States or the Zionists take action, Iran will respond with a new doctrine and new weapons, delivering responses that differ from those of the past,” he said.

Iran’s still-missing Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei delivered his latest written statement following the midterms, warning that America’s days are numbered.

“The process of the US’s collapse has accelerated,” he said.

He then referred to the US as the “Great Satan” and vowed the Iran will never surrender.

The officials’ warnings were echoed around by Iranian broadcasters who mocked the president over the stunning losses across the nation while failing to secure a clear win in the war.

“Trump failed at ⁠regime change in Iran but he succeeded in Texas,” one of the state-run news outlets joked — parroting a post that went viral on X Tuesday night.

Iran does not have free and fair elections — all candidates must be approved by the Supreme Leader for religious purity.

Freedom House ranks Iran as one of the least free nations in the world — behind even Russia.

Prior to the US elections, Iranian officials published an open letter to American voters urging them to rebuke Trump and the war, with reports emerging that Tehran was also trying to use the war and high gas prices to hurt Republican’s chances.

Senior Iranian officials also confirmed that Tehran was deliberately prolonging talks to weaken Trump’s position in the peace discussion, Reuters reported.

stories.title: Israel’s election commission rejects Netanyahu claims of voting fraud
stories.dek: Move comes after attorney general blocks Shin Bet call to interrogate politicians from Palestinian-led parties Israel’s election commission on Wednesday confirmed the final results of last week’s vote…
stories.content:
The Israeli president, Isaac Herzog (right), receives official results of the general election from the chair of the Central Elections Committee, Noam Sohlberg. Photograph: Abir Sultan/EPA View image in fullscreen The Israeli president, Isaac Herzog (right), receives official results of the general election from the chair of the Central Elections Committee, Noam Sohlberg. Photograph: Abir Sultan/EPA Israel Israel’s election commission rejects Netanyahu claims of voting fraud Move comes after attorney general blocks Shin Bet call to interrogate politicians from Palestinian-led parties

Israel’s election commission on Wednesday confirmed the final results of last week’s vote that stripped Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition of its governing majority, rejecting claims of mass fraud promoted by the prime minister.

The main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, said Netanyahu had launched a “pogrom against democracy” in attempting to hold on to power by discrediting valid votes and weaponising security forces against parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel .

Hours earlier, Israel’s attorney general said she had blocked a demand from the Shin Bet security service to interrogate senior politicians from the Palestinian-led parties because she had not been presented with any evidence of wrongdoing.

“In a country governed by the rule of law, neither citizens nor elected officials can be interrogated without evidence that justifies doing so,” Gali Baharav-Miara said in a statement, after Haaretz reported on the attempt to target four politicians.

Election authorities on Wednesday presented the final results to the president, Isaac Herzog, after rejecting allegations they had been tainted by large-scale foreign interference and voter fraud.

“The review found no evidence of irregularities that compromised the integrity of the election or affected its results,” the Central Elections Committee said in a statement.

View image in fullscreen People take part in a rally in Tel Aviv calling for the opposition to form a government with the Palestinian-led parties after last week’s general election. Photograph: Jamal Awad/Reuters The body’s chair, Noam Sohlberg, said some “suspicions” were still under investigation but “they do not cast doubt on the election as a whole or justify delaying the election results”.

When the results were handed over, Herzog denounced racist attacks on Palestinian citizens who had turned out to vote at historic rates.

“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said. “I hold Arab society in Israel in great respect. I value its contribution to the country in every area of life, and its desire to integrate.”

Gadi Eisenkot has secured the public support of all the Jewish Israeli opposition parties. Photograph: Paulina Patimer/JNA/Zuma Press/Shutterstock

stories.title: Israeli president accepts certified election results after commission denies voter fraud
stories.dek: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he would begin consultations with party representatives on the formation of a new government after accepting the certified results from last week's parliamentary el…
stories.content:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog speaks with members of the Central Elections Committee on the day he receives the official results of the elections for the 26th Knesset, at the president's residence in Jerusalem on Wednesday. (Olivier Fitoussi/Reuters) Social Sharing Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he would begin consultations with party representatives on the formation of a new government after accepting the certified results from last week's parliamentary elections, effectively pushing aside claims of voter fraud.

Herzog's acceptance on Wednesday of the results as valid dealt a blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's effort to discredit the vote, in which his religious-nationalist bloc lost its majority in the Israeli parliament, or Knesset, while Arab-led parties made historic gains.

Netanyahu and his supporters have repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims that the Arab-led parties had "stolen" the election, possibly with foreign assistance.

The Israeli president is required now to sit down with various party leaders to determine who to name as prime minister-designate — a process that could potentially bring Netanyahu's opponents to power.

Trump claims U.S. will halt $4B US funding to Israel at end of 2026, as midterms underway

Netanyahu's party amplifies unproven claims that Arab-led parties have ‘stolen' Israel's election

Israel's election commission said earlier on Wednesday that after a thorough investigation of all parties' claims of fraud it had found "no evidence of irregularities that compromised the integrity of the election or affected its results."

Netanyahu's Likud party did not respond to a request for comment.

A separate investigation by the Shin Bet intelligence service, which is headed by David Zini, a Netanyahu appointee and loyalist, into allegations of foreign interference in the election is still ongoing.

In a private meeting on Wednesday of the election committee's members, its head, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, read out an intelligence assessment from the Shin Bet saying the agency believed there had been a "widespread phenomenon involving the influx of substantial funds into Israel from foreign states," including from countries hostile toward Israel.

The Shin Bet provided no evidence to explain its assertion. The Associated Press obtained a transcript of the assessment from a person who attended the meeting. The person requested anonymity to discuss a closed-door meeting.

Netanyahu, Eisenkot left jostling for power after Israel's election

The committee has previously said that while claims about foreign actors seeking to influence the election are serious and under investigation, it does not believe that any such interference affected the results, even if it had happened.

stories.title: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”
stories.dek: Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.
stories.content:
Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.

Donald Trump’s big, rapid American AI buildout now faces a major slowdown as voters in yesterday’s elections overwhelmingly supported candidates and measures that favored increasing restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide.

One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects.

In addition to increasing regulations on data centers, voters also backed anti-AI candidates, electing officials vowing crackdowns in key states building out the most data center capacity in the US.

Most notably, Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor race that Axios reported would fundamentally scramble the math on Trump’s AI buildout. According to Bloomberg , Hinojosa’s election has developers facing down the “worst-case scenario.” Texas is the epicenter of the AI boom, Axios noted, and was expected to account for more than 41 percent of added data center capacity in 2028.

Now, Hinojosa plans to delay projects as long as it takes to pass laws “tackling impacts on water, electricity, air, and property rights.” Approximately “13 gigawatts of data center capacity” is now exposed, Bloomberg reported. Gordon Johnson of GLJ Research warned in a note that Texas projects with “power, permits and steel keep going,” but “those with power but no state environmental permits slip 12 to 18 months,” Bloomberg reported. Some projects may leave the state entirely, perhaps moving to Louisiana or Georgia—or perhaps going nowhere.

“She would impose a moratorium until legislation is passed that gives communities a voice, protects household utility bills, and ends the tax incentives for data centers,” Johnson’s note said. “The question now is how long the pause lasts.” As PIMCO head of public policy Libby Cantrill similarly warned, “even if statewide moratoria do not result, we expect to see a lot more sand in the gears of the AI buildout regardless—with more time required to secure permits and other approvals, as well as more concessions that data center developers will have to make.”

stories.title: SLAC scientists find conclusive proof of a mysterious third type of magnetism
stories.dek: For nearly 90 years, scientists believed magnetism fell into just two categories, but researchers have now confirmed a remarkable third type called altermagnetism.
stories.content:
For nearly 90 years, physicists have divided magnetic materials into two main categories: ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Now, scientists have confirmed that a third type exists, revealing a previously unrecognized form of magnetic behavior that could lead to major advances in computing and electronics.

The breakthrough comes from a research team led by the U.S. Department of Energy's SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory. In a study published in Science , the researchers presented compelling experimental evidence for altermagnetism, a distinct magnetic phase that combines important characteristics of the two traditionally recognized types.

"In the past few years, scientists have observed phenomena that don't fit neatly into the ferromagnetism-antiferromagnetism dichotomy," explained lead author Daniel Jost, associate scientist at SLAC and Stanford Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences. "Researchers have been compiling evidence of a third type of magnetism that bridges the qualities of these two classes. We believe our results provide robust experimental confirmation that this third phase -- altermagnetism -- is real."

The team focused on manganese telluride (MnTe), a material that had long been classified as an antiferromagnet. Building on earlier research, the scientists identified direct evidence of chirality, a distinctive asymmetry in the material's magnetic structure. This property resembles the way a spiral staircase or screw twists in a particular direction and provides a crucial signature of altermagnetism.

Beyond its importance for fundamental physics, the finding could help researchers develop magnetic materials with properties suited to future technologies, including advanced memory systems, quantum devices, and more energy-efficient data centers.

Magnetism is familiar from everyday experiences, whether it is a refrigerator magnet holding up a photograph or a compass aligning with Earth's magnetic field. But the physics behind these effects is far more complicated than it appears.

At the atomic level, magnetism is connected to a quantum property of electrons known as spin. Although spin is not literally an electron rotating like a tiny ball, it behaves in certain ways as though the electron has its own angular momentum. Scientists commonly describe the two possible spin orientations as "up" and "down."

When these spins become organized into particular patterns, a material can exhibit magnetic properties. However, that does not necessarily mean it will produce an externally detectable magnetic field.

In ferromagnetic materials, electron spins align in the same direction (up-up-up or down-down-down). Their combined effect produces the familiar magnetic field associated with ordinary magnets. People have used materials with this behavior for thousands of years.

stories.title: Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Agreements and Regional Energy Corridors
stories.dek: A multi-perspective assessment of offshore natural gas transit frameworks, maritime boundary negotiations, and regional stability.
stories.content:
The Eastern Mediterranean basin continues to navigate complex multilateral diplomatic engagements balancing offshore energy exploration with sovereign boundary delimitation. High-level delegations from regional coastal states and European partners are refining frameworks that align pipeline routes with equitable maritime economic zones.

Key Perspectives & Strategic Dimensions:
1. Energy Transit Security: Multilateral agreements between Mediterranean states prioritize uninterrupted transit of natural gas to Southern European ports, diversifying continental supply lines.
2. Maritime Boundary Delimitation: Diplomatic mediators emphasize that long-term maritime stability necessitates transparent dispute-resolution mechanisms that account for sovereign continental shelf claims.
3. Regional Economic Interdependence: Joint infrastructure investments in subsea interconnectors create economic mutual interest, offering pragmatic stabilization incentives across diverse stakeholders.
stories.whyItMatters: Directly impacts the economic stability, energy infrastructure, and security landscape across the Levant and Mediterranean.

stories.title: Sub-Microsecond Spin Dynamics in Diamond NV Centers: Benchmarking Cavity QED and Coherence Limits
stories.dek: Mitigating dipolar spin-spin dephasing and hyperfine bath interactions in dense diamond NV ensembles via Floquet driving.
stories.content:
Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond remain the preeminent solid-state platform for room-temperature quantum metrology and nanoscale magnetic resonance. Scaling from isolated defects to dense ensembles requires overcoming collective dephasing from the surrounding 13C nuclear spin bath.

Recent breakthroughs utilizing microwave cavity coupling and Floquet dynamical decoupling extend the effective coherence time (T2*) by an order of magnitude.

Key Technical Highlights:
1. Cooperative Purcell Enhancement: Dense NV ensembles entering the collective strong coupling regime demonstrate cavity-mediated coherence preservation.
2. Suppression of Spin-Diffusion Loss: Operating within crystallographic symmetry subspaces eliminates cross-axis relaxation.
3. Room-Temperature Sensing: Sustained microsecond coherence enables sub-picotesla magnetic field sensitivities for single-cell NMR.
stories.whyItMatters: Informs room-temperature diamond quantum magnetometry, microwave cavity loading, and advanced Floquet decoupling protocols in spin dynamics.

stories.source: Innatera & Edge AI Insights • 5 min read
stories.title: Sub-Milliwatt Neuromorphic Microcontrollers Shift Real-Time AI Inference to the Edge
stories.dek: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) on silicon processors achieve microsecond response times at sub-milliwatt power budgets.
stories.content:
The paradigm of routing sensor telemetry to centralized cloud servers is rapidly transitioning to on-device neuromorphic microcontrollers. Utilizing event-driven spiking neural architectures, silicon accelerators process acoustic and vibration patterns with near-zero latency.

Key Highlights:
1. In-Memory Processing: Spiking architectures circumvent the classical von Neumann memory bottleneck, consuming less than 1 mW.
2. Zero Cloud Exposure: Sensitive sensor streams remain strictly local, guaranteeing privacy and continuous operation during network blackouts.
3. Predictive Maintenance: Deployed microcontrollers classify industrial vibrations and structural stress in real time.
stories.whyItMatters: Enables zero-latency, private, on-device anomaly detection and vibration monitoring without cloud roundtrips.

stories.title: Circadian Photonic Priming and Equanimity in Demanding Research
stories.dek: Aligning 90-minute ultradian deep work blocks with natural circadian rhythms and secular Buddhist non-reactivity.
stories.content:
Sustained high-level analytical performance requires deliberate biological pacing. Structuring the day around 90-minute ultradian cycles followed by brief decompression intervals prevents cognitive fatigue.

Core Evidence-Based Habits:
1. Photonic Lock: Direct outdoor light exposure within 45 minutes of waking aligns the suprachiasmatic nucleus master clock.
2. Ultradian Block: Dedicate the primary 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM window to pure theoretical derivation before checking correspondence.
3. Secular Equanimity (Dhammapada 81): 'Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.'
stories.whyItMatters: Protects cognitive bandwidth and prevents attentional fragmentation during demanding laboratory derivations.

papers.title: Low-Field J-Coupling Spectroscopy Measured with a Diamond Nitrogen Vacancy Spectrometer
papers.authors: Stephen J. DeVience, John W. Blanchard, Camille G. McDonnell et al.
papers.tldr: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields. NV spin states can be initialized and read out optically with high spatial resolution, enabling detection of pL-scale volumes of nuclear spins.
takeaways: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields.

Using Coherently Averaged Synchronized Readout (CASR), standard NMR spectroscopy techniques such as free decay, spin echo, and PGSE have been performed with Hz-scale spectral resolution using NV-diamond sensors.

We acquire initial NV-NMR measurements of T$_1$, T$_2$, and Overhauser DNP in glycerol before advancing to SEDOR spectroscopy of methanol-$^{13}$C and a methanol-$^{13}$C/acetonitrile-2-$^{13}$C mixture at sample volumes $\sim$50 pL, in which we demonstrate measurement of $^1J_\text{CH}$ couplings and resolution between species.

papers.title: Aging dynamics and generalized superposition principles in carbon black-carboxymethylcellulose hydrogels
papers.authors: Gauthier Legrand, Guilhem P. Baeza, Jarno L. Waeterloos et al.
papers.tldr: Aqueous dispersions of hydrophobic carbon black (CB) particles can be stabilized by carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), forming CB-CMC hydrogels whose microstructure is controlled by the relative CB-to-polymer content. At low CMC content, CB particles form a percolated, electrically conductive network, whereas at higher polymer content, CB particles act as isolated physical crosslinkers within an electrically insulating polymer matrix [see Legrand \textit{et al.}, Macromolecules 56, 2298-2308 (2023)].
takeaways: Aqueous dispersions of hydrophobic carbon black (CB) particles can be stabilized by carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), forming CB-CMC hydrogels whose microstructure is controlled by the relative CB-to-polymer content.

At low CMC content, CB particles form a percolated, electrically conductive network, whereas at higher polymer content, CB particles act as isolated physical crosslinkers within an electrically insulating polymer matrix [see Legrand \textit{et al.}, Macromolecules 56, 2298-2308 (2023)].
Finally, time-resolved rheo-USAXS measurements performed during shear-rate cycles reveal structural rearrangements of CB particles and clusters that correlate with rheological hysteresis.

papers.title: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases
papers.authors: Ryota Nakai, Taozhi Guo, Shinsei Ryu
papers.tldr: Chiral Floquet phases support quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized. In this Letter, we establish a complementary phenomenon, which we call Hilbert-space pumping: under a boundary condition twisted by time translation, a part of the boundary Hilbert space, of quantized dimension, is transferred between the opposite boundaries.
takeaways: Chiral Floquet phases support quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized.

For noninteracting fermions, the number of transferred boundary modes is determined by the winding number, as we show analytically for the boundary dynamics and numerically for the anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator.

For interacting systems whose boundary dynamics is a quantum cellular automaton, the transferred dimension is set by the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index: the twisted boundary Floquet operator is the Floquet operator on a tilted time slice, whose Hilbert-space dimension is multiplied by the index for each period of twist.

papers.title: Nonlinearity-Induced Suppression of Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators
papers.tldr: Topological insulators can host chiral, disorder-robust edge states that dissipate energy when coupled to an external bath. We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath.
takeaways: Topological insulators can host chiral, disorder-robust edge states that dissipate energy when coupled to an external bath.
We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath.

Although moderate nonlinearity enhances dissipation due to mode mixing, increasing the nonlinear strength to an optimal value dramatically suppresses dissipation by forming highly localized traveling edge solitons.

papers.title: Strong Thermal Conductivity Suppression in Isotope Purified Single Crystal Diamond with Phonon Scatterings of Color Centers
papers.authors: Jinwen Liu, Junliang Fan, Zimu Jiang et al.
papers.tldr: The thermal conductivity of natural diamond can be further improved by ~50% by eliminating isotope impurity to obtain pure 12C diamond. However, unlike isolated point defects, how color centers scatter phonons and correspondingly limit the thermal conductivity remain poorly understood.
takeaways: The thermal conductivity of natural diamond can be further improved by ~50% by eliminating isotope impurity to obtain pure 12C diamond.
However, unlike isolated point defects, how color centers scatter phonons and correspondingly limit the thermal conductivity remain poorly understood.

Here, we report the thermal conductivities of two isotope-purified diamond with different Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color center concentrations, confirmed by photoluminescence (PL) and secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS).
